P1.evidence: Application acknowledged rather than read back — 'I see that you already filled a few things in your form, but I just want to go over everything with you.' Two-part frame, missing what's-in-the-way and what-you-need. Agreement given. Open question ran: 'take me through, like what can we potentially help you out with, Brett?' Also handled the time budget well and offered a rebook — 'these meetings run for like 45 minutes usually, I don't know if you have that time' — which mattered, because the prospect capped it at thirty minutes and the call ran fifteen.

P2.evidence: The one clean hit is also the only time in this batch the rep asks it: 'What do you do for work?' — answered, tech investor. The injury question was asked in a usable form — 'mobility-wise, are you already in the best shape there for yourself, or is there things that you're struggling with, anything that we should know about?' — and produced the torn shoulder, but nothing followed it: no duration, no severity, no question about the deferred surgery or what he has been advised. Everything else is absent. Age, weight and weight history were volunteered inside his opening monologue and never asked. Diet was never asked despite fat loss being the headline goal, and the GLP-1 disclosure drew no response at all. No training week, no sleep, no energy.

P3.evidence: Goals were asked directly and pinned to a number — 'take me through your goal, what you specifically want to get to' — producing 176 to 170 and the toned-and-defined target. The bridge was asked well: 'you're already in the best shape, now you just want to get a little bit better. So what's the reason for you that you want to push that extra bit?' The reflect-back landed and was confirmed. But the answer to the bridge stayed at the level of momentum logic and the rep did not push past it — no feeling question, no who-else-does-this-impact, nothing about family, identity or legacy. Credit for one good off-script move: 'are there any other ways that you can think of that would potentially make you fail?', which is a genuinely useful question.

P4.evidence: No past-attempts sequence was run. Everything known about his history — the running, the compound lifts, the GLP-1, the Peloton subscription, the TikTok-copied kettlebell sessions — arrived unprompted in his opening answer and was never followed up. The ways-you-could-fail question did partial duty for the blocker question, and he named the gap himself as programming and variety, but the rep took that at face value rather than testing it. Nobody asked why the free version has stopped working for him, which was the available wedge.

P5.evidence: No consequence frame. The prospect actually supplied the frame himself — 'if we're not trying to get better, then you're bound to stagnate and move back' — and it was not picked up. No two-year projection, no settle question, no line in the sand. Given he had told the story of gaining sixteen pounds after an injury and being shocked at himself in January, there was a specific and recent cost of inaction sitting in plain view.

P6.evidence: Never ran. Price was disclosed at 00:10:25 because the prospect demanded it, with no belief question and no all-in question beforehand. The prospect had also flagged the risk explicitly — 'I'm not committing to do it either, right?' — which is precisely the state the commitment check exists to resolve before a number is spoken.

P11.evidence: A soft close was attempted on the $200 tier and nothing was collected — no link sent on the call, details promised by email afterwards, decision deferred a week. Steps two to four do not apply to that tier and were not reachable in any case.

objection_plays.detail: The clearest money trigger in the batch — 'that's more than I'm, like, totally transparently' — and not one move ran. No isolate, no should-versus-how reframe, no permission ask, none of the financial picture. The rep agreed with the objection inside one turn and was pitching a $200 product within sixty seconds. This is the same prospect who had just described himself as a tech investor, so capacity was never the issue and the play was never given a chance to find out what was.

Script gap, and the same one that ended the Chad call two days earlier — a prospect who wants the price before the discovery sequence. Here the rep did the opposite and complied immediately: 'Maybe we just start there. Like, what does the program cost?' produced a number at minute ten of a fifteen-minute call, before goals depth, consequence or commitment existed. Two calls, two opposite improvisations, both lost. The playbook needs a sanctioned answer for this.

Clinical gap. A torn left shoulder with surgery deferred and movements already being self-restricted is a live contraindication question for a kettlebell programme, and there is no scripted path. The rep's entire response was 'so you want to make sure, of course, your shoulder doesn't get worse', and he then recommended the unsupervised tier.

No play exists for the trial request either — 'can I try it out for like a month or two weeks?'. The rep improvised a workaround by reframing a cancellable month as a trial, which is reasonable, but it is an invented mechanism rather than a sanctioned one.

notes: The best-qualified prospect in the batch and the least process applied to him: fifteen minutes, no baseline to speak of, no consequence frame, no commitment check, and a price given on demand at minute ten. When the price landed the rep did not defend it for a single turn. Whatever the right answer is to 'tell me the price first', conceding the entire offer thirty seconds later is not it.
